stringing_variation.val_note: VAL is the primary development-domain generalization evidence; training-set performance is descriptive only, not generalization proof.
stringing_variation.caveat: Determining which class (A/B/C/D) is best supported is a judgment based on the reported numbers; no automated claim is made.

darkness_audit.correlation_note: Negative correlation would indicate darker normal recordings trend toward higher FPR. Correlation over ~recordings is descriptive and does NOT establish causality or semantic OOD.
darkness_audit.caveat: Brightness is a proxy, not proof of semantic domain shift; no causal claim is made.

brightness_buckets.method: Bucket boundaries derived ONLY from the TRAIN normal brightness distribution (tertiles). No official TEST statistic was used. Explicitly avoiding tiny buckets; if a bucket is empty it is reported as empty rather than forcing a split.

under_extrusion.caveat: Comparison to stringing is descriptive; session count is NOT claimed as the sole explanation for any performance difference.

conclusions.note: Official test set contains no spaghetti frames, so frozen test spaghetti performance cannot be measured and no generalization conclusion is possible. No spaghetti performance estimate is invented. Spaghetti remains a future-data priority.

catastrophic_fn.note: Existing final-test observation; documented for context only.

high_fp.from_stage8: high-confidence false positives (p>0.98) despite pure normal label
high_fp.note: Existing final-test observation; documented for context only.

documented_test_observations.firewall_note: Official test statistics are displayed for context ONLY. No test statistic defines a brightness bucket, selects a threshold, determines acquisition, sets session counts, or triggers a model change.

image_distribution.method: Deterministic non-learned statistics only; no PCA, clustering, or learned embeddings are used. Analysis is intentionally kept simple.

stringing.detail: Prefer genuinely independent stringing sessions (distinct dates, objects, recording conditions, optical/camera conditions) over additional frames from existing recordings, because independent sessions add provenance/domain coverage whereas extra frames from one session only add within-session redundancy.

dark_normal.detail: Add normal-domain images spanning the brightness range, especially darker conditions, to broaden coverage.

spaghetti.detail: Spaghetti has only 5 training recordings / 191 train frames and no test frames; it remains a future-data priority with no measurable frozen-test baseline.

under_extrusion.detail: Under-extrusion has the most diverse training domain; treat it as the comparison/control for the stringing decision.

classifications_defined.insufficient_evidence: cannot conclude from available TRAIN/VAL data

future_split_design.principle: Session atomicity preserved; never split frames of one session across sets.
future_split_design.hold_out_note: The official Experiment 1 test set remains FROZEN. A future targeted experiment should use sessions reserved across dates/objects/lighting for its held-out generalization set; do not reuse Experiment 1 frozen test frames as training or validation data.

retraining_gate.B_first_data_to_add: Independent stringing sessions across new dates/objects/conditions ('5-10 minimum, 15-20 strong' from Stage 9); plus targeted dark-normal sessions and any available spaghetti sessions.
retraining_gate.C_still_missing: Evidence that added stringing diversity reduces stringing FNR and that added dark-normal coverage reduces normal FPR, without regressing overall F1, as measured on FROZEN independent evaluation sets.
retraining_gate.D_minimum_useful_experiment: Collect proposed new sessions; freeze a new split by session with a held-out set; retrain the same architecture on the expanded training set; evaluate on the FROZEN Experiment 1 test at 0.50 and 0.65.
retraining_gate.E_result_that_justifies_retraining: Stringing FNR improves by >=5pp (ideally >=10pp) with no F1 regression, dark-normal FPR falls, and the held-out set performs comparably to the frozen test.
notes: No architecture change is recommended unless the evidence specifically supports it.
Temporal/FSM logic is NOT proposed as a solution to the underlying frame-classification problem.
